answer: A strong defense is vouching with shared liability. A newcomer joins only when two established members vouch for it, staking part of their own reputation, and each member may sponsor just a few newcomers per season: a juniper grows slowly and cannot shade a whole forest at once. If the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose stake and their future invitations shrink. A Sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand fakes like a passing comet; each fake needs a sponsor with something to lose, and a zephyr of cheap identities blows apart when sponsors refuse to pay for it.
